STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall visible. Flat plate, square.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, medium-large, so about 26 cm.
b) Reference: the pizza/lasagna-style slices are roughly 11-12 cm long each. The plate spans about 2.2-2.4 slice lengths across, which gives about 25-27 cm.
Both cues agree: width about 26 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Salad greens (spinach, mixed greens, kale): the greens cover most of the right and bottom half of the plate, a fairly thin but dense layer, roughly 2-2.5 cm thick at the mound. Footprint about 45% of 676 cm² ≈ 300 cm². Average thickness about 1.5 cm → volume ≈ 450 ml. Raw leafy greens at 0.15 g/ml ≈ 65 g. Several leaves are piled, so take about 70 g.
- Pizza/flatbread slices (two wedges): each wedge is about 11 cm long, 4 cm wide, 1.5 cm thick, so about 60 cm³ of crust-and-topping per wedge, at about 0.6 g/ml on average ≈ 35 g each. Two wedges ≈ 70 g... but the cheese and meat topping are denser, so take roughly 90 g for both wedges together.
- Tomato slice: one thin slice, about 6 cm diameter, 0.5 cm thick ≈ 14 cm³ → about 10 g.
- Cheese (melted mozzarella on one wedge): a thin layer, about 20 cm² × 0.4 cm ≈ 8 ml → about 8 g.
- Olives or mushrooms (a few small pieces near the bottom): about 3 pieces at ~4 g each ≈ 12 g; treat as mushrooms ≈ 15 g.
- Red onion slivers and dressing: small amount, about 5 g onion, dressing traces about 5 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No rice or grain base. The greens and wedges sit on the plate surface, so no large hidden layer. The total stays well under 300 g, consistent with a few items on a large plate.

- Pizza wedges (crust, sauce, meat, cheese): 260 kcal/100 g
- Tomato: 18 kcal/100 g
- Melted mozzarella: 300 kcal/100 g

- Red onion: 40 kcal/100 g
- Dressing: 300 kcal/100 g (small amount)

Estimated total: about 250 g, about 0.5 kcal per gram overall... computed per item below.
